Situation1: There is a scheduled family gathering on the calendar.
Expectation2: Adhere to site protocols and work effectively as part of the team.
Situation2: The mandatory daily pre-work safety briefing is starting in two minutes.
Story: I glance at the clock on my phone, my hands still rough from yesterday’s work. The family group chat is buzzing—my daughter reminding everyone about the gathering today, my grandson asking if I’ll bring his favorite cookies. I promised I’d be there, and I want nothing more than to see their faces, to hear their laughter. But as I tuck my phone away, the foreman’s voice booms across the site: “Safety briefing in two minutes! Everyone, let’s go!” I know how strict the rules are—missing the briefing means I can’t work today, and the team is counting on me to help finish the foundation. My boots are caked with mud, my heart heavy with the weight of two worlds. I can almost smell the coffee at my daughter’s house, but the clang of metal and the shouts of my coworkers pull me back. I stand at the edge of the site, torn, the expectations of family and work pressing in from both sides, unsure which way to turn.
